policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakhstan prior-visa baseline after the 2026 seasonal waiver
policies.summary: The current Kazakhstan guidance expressly requires a visa outside the 1 May–1 October 2026 seasonal waiver. The already recorded ordinary passport-only prior-visa baseline therefore applies from 2 October, with consular issuance and the published short-stay visa C ceiling.
conditions: A Montenegro visa must be obtained before travel through a competent diplomatic or consular mission; the Kazakhstan page identifies the Bulgarian embassy in Kazakhstan as an alternative where a Montenegro mission cannot be approached.

Article 7 separately provides a document-conditioned route for qualifying Schengen, Australian, Japanese, Canadian, New Zealand, Irish, US or UK visas, qualifying residence permits, or APEC business travel cards: up to 30 days and no longer than the supporting document remains valid. This is not a Kazakh passport-only waiver.
The short-stay visa C limit is a ceiling, not an automatic grant of 90 days. The issued visa, permitted purpose, entry conditions and admission decision determine the actual stay.
The general travel document rule requires issuance within the preceding ten years and validity for at least three months after planned departure, with the MFA's stated emergency exceptions.

The 2 October boundary preserves the adopted seasonal decision's 1 October endpoint and the existing reviewed policy. No extension or electronically issued visa route was established in this fresh read; work, residence and special travel documents remain separate.

allowedStays.label: Short-stay visa C: up to 90 days in 180 days from first entry, subject to the issued visa
notes: The MFA counts the period from first entry and states a maximum stay. Actual permission can be shorter; this is not visa validity or an unconditional 90-day entitlement.

policies.title: Montenegro: Belarus and Russia 30-day waiver through 31 October 2026
policies.summary: Article 3a and both current nationality pages preserve visa-free ordinary-passport entry, transit and stays up to 30 days through 31 October 2026. The 24 September Government follow-up reiterates the visa requirement from 1 November.
conditions: A valid travel document issued by the competent Belarusian or Russian authority is required, pursuant to the reciprocal-travel agreements referenced by Article 3a.
The 30-day allowance is limited by the published waiver endpoint; it does not establish a right to continue visa-free stay beyond 31 October 2026 or to enter under this route from 1 November.
The Government's September treaty-termination follow-up reiterates the ordinary-passport change. It does not establish any extension of this waiver.
General document validity and admission requirements remain applicable. Work, residence, diplomatic/service documents and Article 7 supporting-document exceptions are separate routes.

allowedStays.label: Up to 30 days under the waiver ending 31 October 2026
notes: The exemption's endpoint does not establish permission to remain visa-free beyond 31 October 2026.

policies.title: Montenegro: Saudi and Turkish 30-day waiver through 31 October 2026
policies.summary: Article 1a and both current nationality pages allow ordinary Saudi and Turkish passport holders visa-free entry, transit and stays up to 30 days through 31 October 2026. The current Turkish page expressly identifies the 1 November change.
conditions: A valid travel document issued by the competent Saudi or Turkish authority is required.
The 30-day allowance is limited by the published waiver endpoint; it does not establish a right to continue visa-free stay beyond 31 October 2026 or to enter under this route from 1 November.
The contemplated new Turkish diplomatic/service/special-passport agreement is not an ordinary-passport exemption and is not represented as an adopted replacement.
General document validity and admission requirements remain applicable. Work, residence and Article 7 supporting-document exceptions are separate routes.

allowedStays.label: Up to 30 days under the waiver ending 31 October 2026
notes: The exemption's endpoint does not establish permission to remain visa-free beyond 31 October 2026.

policies.title: Montenegro: Belarus, Russia, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye require visas from 1 November 2026
policies.summary: The MFA's express 1 November visa requirement, the regulation and the Government's September treaty follow-up reconfirm the existing future ordinary passport-only prior-visa baseline for these four nationalities. The short-stay visa C ceiling remains subject to the actual visa granted.
conditions: This future rule does not displace the current 30-day waiver through 31 October 2026. From 1 November, ordinary passport-only visitors require a Montenegro visa before travel.

Visa issuance remains through the competent diplomatic or consular authority. The current Russian and Turkish pages list VFS filing centres; application assistance is not electronic issuance. The July MFA notice describes eVisas as a future system project.

Article 7 separately preserves qualifying third-country visa, residence-permit and APEC-card entry for up to 30 days, no longer than the supporting document's validity. These traveller-document exceptions are not nationality-wide waivers.

A short-stay visa C cannot authorize more than 90 days in 180 days counted from first entry. The actual visa and admission decision can authorize less; the ceiling is not an automatic stay entitlement or visa-validity period.
The general travel document rule requires issuance within the preceding ten years and validity for at least three months after planned departure, with the MFA's stated emergency exceptions.

The September Government follow-up proposes a separate Turkish diplomatic/service/special-passport agreement. It does not preserve the ordinary Turkish passport waiver; work, residence, special documents and final admission remain separate.

allowedStays.label: Short-stay visa C: up to 90 days in 180 days from first entry, subject to the issued visa
notes: The MFA counts the period from first entry and states a maximum stay. Actual permission can be shorter; this is not visa validity or an unconditional 90-day entitlement.
